blocks.text: Run a pinned Qdrant image with named volumes for storage and snapshots, configure it via `QDRANT__SECTION__KEY` env vars, and create collections idempotently at app startup, failing on dimension mismatch.

blocks.code:
qdrant:
  image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.4          # pin; check current release
  environment:
    QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY: ${QDRANT_API_KEY:?required}
  volumes: [qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage, qdrant_snapshots:/qdrant/snapshots]
  ports: ["127.0.0.1:6333:6333"]        # 6333 REST/dashboard, 6334 gRPC
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/6333' || exit 1"]

async def ensure_collection(client, name, dim):
    if not await client.collection_exists(name):
        await client.create_collection(name, vectors_config=VectorParams(size=dim, distance=Distance.COSINE))
        return
    existing = (await client.get_collection(name)).config.params.vectors.size
    if existing != dim:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: dim {existing} != {dim}, re-index required")

items: Named volumes, not bind mounts: Qdrant warns that some filesystems (Windows/WSL, network FS) lack the POSIX semantics it needs and can corrupt data.
Back up with the snapshot API, not file copies of a live store.
Minimal images may lack curl: check the tools before writing healthchecks.

blocks.text: An API key passed via env is visible in docker inspect. That's fine locally; inject it from a secret store in production.

Q: "How do you run Qdrant safely in Compose?" A: "A pinned image, named volumes for storage and snapshots, loopback-only ports, an API key even locally, a TCP healthcheck, snapshot-based backups, and idempotent collection creation that fails fast when the configured dimension doesn't match."
